title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws
read_level: full (PDF via pdftotext; main text, tables 1-4, limitations; appendices not read in detail)
why_wsp: GPT-6 Astra audits trained clinical models (incl. neural networks) by querying predictions through a NumPy calculator tool, writing a surrogate and a list of flaws; weights are not given except in a secondary white-box condition on two networks, so it is the query-only counterpart to WSP reading.
domain: clinical prediction models (International Stroke Trial; death/dependency outcomes)
editor: GPT-6 Astra via Codex CLI, reasoning effort max (auditor, no edits)
target: 32 tabular models: logistic regression, explainable boosting machine, gradient-boosted trees, neural network (1-2 hidden layers, 8-32 tanh units) x 2 outcomes x (1 clean + 3 flawed)
interface: code/tensor tools (calculator running NumPy with predict(X) only; white-box condition loads weights)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (agentic queries within one run; median 12 tool calls)

headline_results.quote: reproduced the audited models’ log-odds on the test inputs with a mean R2 of 0.976 (median over runs 0.982), against 0.959 for the analyst’s surrogate
The LLM found the planted flaw in 69 of 72 runs (96%). The three runs of a model always agreed (intraclass correlation 1.00), so the effective sample size was 24 and the 95% interval 80% to 99%
The audit script found all 24 planted flaws, and none of its 45 reports failed the check
Of the 1,089 reports that could be checked, 655 (60%; 95% CI 53% to 67%) failed the pre-specified check
68 of the LLM’s relationships held (11%; 95% CI 9% to 14%), against 28 of the scan’s 101 (28%; 20% to 37%) ... and 20 of 348 random pairs (6%; 4% to 9%)
With the weights of the two clean networks loaded in the tool, the mean R2 was 0.951, against 0.947 for the same networks through queries alone
separated those that held from those that did not only weakly (C statistic 0.66, Brier score 0.30)

cost.claim: Time and tool calls per black-box run
cost.quote: A black-box run took a median of 16 minutes (longest 32) and 12 tool calls (range 7 to 21)

baselines_and_controls: Analyst's 42-term additive surrogate; purpose-written query-only audit script; regression scan; models' strongest interactions (H statistic, computed post hoc); positive control (established factors) and negative control (random pairs); 8 clean models mixed with 24 flawed; white-box vs black-box on two networks.
runs_and_variance: 3 independent runs per model (96 black-box, 6 white-box); bootstrap CI for R2 difference (+0.017, 95% CI 0.016 to 0.018); Wilson intervals on effective sample size accounting for intraclass correlation.
verification: Pre-registered (private repo) judging rules applied by program; blinding guard on tool; all tool calls inspected.
memorization_vs_reasoning: Paper notes the trial is public and much analysed so "the LLM may know its results; this bears on the relationships it proposed more than on the audit". Cites own prior study that ability came "from computation, not from access to weights".
limitations_stated: One LLM, one dataset (public, possibly known to the LLM); flaws artificial, large and of three announced kinds; pre-specified check mismatched to report form, post hoc classes; scan given shorter list; runs not independent (24 effective); plan in private repo, amended before first run; two deviations computed after results.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog, Nov 2026)
Liu and Yang, Computation, not weight access (arXiv 2611.07847)
Nusrat and Nusrat, WSP for auditing clinical decision networks (arXiv 2611.05341)
notes_for_survey: Query-only control for WSP reading claims: planted-flaw detection reaches 96% of runs but a purpose-written script also finds all 24; 60% of other reported problems fail the pre-specified check. White-box weight access did not improve surrogate fidelity on the two networks tested.
